observation_summary: The compiler reported an incorrect type name in a 'property never defined' error message. Specifically, it reported the name of the property holder (e.g., 'C3.c2_') instead of the actual type of the object (e.g., 'C2').
reasoning_summary: The fix involved reordering the logic within the 'getReadableJSTypeName' method. By moving the dereferencing logic and the check for constructor/prototype types to the beginning of the method, the compiler correctly identifies the underlying type before falling back to the qualified name. This is a procedural correction to the algorithm used to resolve and format type names for error reporting.
evidence_used: The fix reorders the logic in 'getReadableJSTypeName' to prioritize dereferencing and constructor type identification.
The bug report states the error message was 'Property prop never defined on C3.c2_' instead of 'C2', indicating a failure in the type name resolution algorithm.
The diff shows the logic for determining the type name was moved to occur before the fallback to 'n.getQualifiedName()'.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not about setting a wrong value or initialization, but about changing the order of operations in a method to correctly resolve a type name.
The fix does not involve changing method signatures or API contracts between components.
